namlich is an answer marker which can be used to answer a specific question or to answer a more general question about the relevance of the information provided by the previous utterance.

namlich is not only an explanative particle, but also a specificational particle.

the German particle namelijk, traditionally described as a discourse particle with a specificative and an explanative function, is a discourse marker signalling a short answer to an implicit question.
our approach to namlich is based on the idea of a discourse particle which is not a discourse marker, but a discourse marker which is not a conjunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not only concerned with the question of how the two readings are related but also with the question of what the relation between namlich and its two readings is.
namlich is an answer particle which has a specificational and a non-specificational use, depending on whether it is used to answer a specificational or a non-specificational question, respectively.
namlich is not an adverbial or an adverb but a discourse particle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the specificational reading of namlich can be accounted for by the same mechanisms that are used for its explanative reading, and that there is no need to posit a specificational meaning for namlich in addition to an explanative one.
the specificational reading of namlich is not a semantic property but rather a consequence of the discourse pragmatic function of namlich.
the distinction between specification and explanation is not a semantic distinction but a pragmatic one.
